text:
noah: Quick sync — want to finalize a compact benchmark narrative for the launch: 3 visuals, one short-form post, webinar slot, and simple lead routing. Keep it ops-friendly.
sophia: yes. propose we anchor visuals around user-facing cost (cost / 1k tokens) and two latency views (median + tail). short and punchy.
lucas: agree. also add a tiny appendix chart showing dedicated pool $/vCPU-hour so infra teams can eyeball ops cost.
zoe: timeline? I can craft the social post + landing copy if visuals specs are clear.
noah: target: draft visuals by Mon EOD, copy Tue. webinar Wed/Thu.
sophia: visual specs idea: Chart 1 (unit econ):
```
x: model variant
y: $ per 1k tokens (hosted)
annotations: percent delta vs baseline
points: default, quantized, cached
```
lucas: Chart 2 (latency distribution):
```
x: percentile (50,75,90,95,99)
y: latency (ms)
lines: short-chat, long-agent
callout: p95 SLA line
```
zoe: Chart 3 (ops-slice):
```
rows: interactive, batch-embed
metric: cost per 1k tokens, median latency
bars: reserved vs autoscale
```
noah: marketing copy directions (two tones):
- Tone A (practical): "Bench-backed ops: predictable latency and clear unit economics for production LLMs."
- Tone B (customer POV): "Faster responses, lower bill — see where savings come from for your app."
sophia: short social hook suggestion: "We measured median + tail latency across real slices — and cut unit costs by up to 55% for common workloads. Sample calc inside."
lucas: sample calc (for sales cheat-sheet): "Baseline hosted: $0.00045 per token => $450 per 1M tokens. With quantization + caching: ~55% lower => $202 per 1M tokens. Show both per-1k and per-1M on the sheet."
zoe: inbound routing rules (simple):
- auto-tag "bench" if user uploads prompts or requests demo
- enterprise route if expected monthly tokens > 20M or requests private deploy
- webinar RSVP -> nurture track with bench CSV and sample chart
noah: webinar pitch (one-liner): "Real slices, real numbers: how we measure latency and cost for production apps." CTA: "Bring a prompt set 1"
sophia: bench-bot wiring: can we have an auto-attach so when someone tags "bench" it runs a micro-pass and returns a CSV + PNG? minimal UX: `/bench quick --model default --n=1000`
bench-bot: feature note: quick-run returns: CSV (per-request metrics), summary JSON, and PNGs. flags: --cache on/off, --quant on/off. use `/bench quick --help` for options.
lucas: for the appendix: add a 1-row table that maps common app patterns to recommended configs (chat -> batch small, agent -> keep KV cache warm, embeddings -> async batching).
zoe: copy drafts I'll try: subject lines for email: "Your app7s latency, in numbers" and "Reduce inference spend without slowing users"
noah: deliverables list: visuals (A/B colorways), one social post, sales cheat-sheet calc, webinar blurb, routing bullets, bench quick command examples. Keep copy <=2 lines each.
sophia: pairing: lucas + bench infra will run the quick microbench and drop PNGs. zoe will mock the landing with placeholder charts.
lucas: quick-run example command to share with folks:
```bash
/bench quick --model rwd-small --slices interactive,batch --tokens 2000 --cache on --quant off --out=./bench_quick
```
zoe: gentle note for copy: avoid exact numeric claims in hero; use ranges. e.g. "up to 55% lower unit cost" vs exact percent unless appendix backs it.
noah: agreed. let's keep hero conservative. sophia — can you post the chart PNGs here once done? aiming for Mon EOD.
sophia: will do. bench-bot queued the run. ETA ~30m.
bench-bot: queued 2 quick jobs. expected completion in ~28m. outputs will include CSV + 2 PNGs + short summary text.
lucas: great. I'll review kernels if we need to tune perf for the long-agent slice.
zoe: thanks team. I'll have landing copy draft by Tue morning. short and clip-ready.
noah: perfect. close loop here once visuals drop and we can move to copy iterations.
